The Acquisition Almanac · 30 Clubs · 2015–2026

Who Actually Finds Talent?

Built from 9,105 draft selections, 638,952 transactions, and Baseball-Reference WAR through .

OTR — the Organizational Talent Rating. One number for how well a front office finds talent, on a plus scale: 100 = league average, 128 = 28% above. Three pillars, each indexed to 100: D+ Discovery (draft surplus over slot + international pipeline), T+ Dealing (the net trade ledger), S+ Salvage (reclamations, waivers, Rule 5). Pillars are weighted by their real share of the league's found-WAR pool — the formula earns its weights from the data. The headline blends the full 2015–present era (70%) with the last three seasons (30%); ▲▼ marks a club whose recent finding runs hot or cold versus its era self by more than half a league standard deviation (±8 OTR points). Free-agent spending is excluded throughout: this rates finding, not buying.

The receipts. Every meaningful acquisition (0.5+ WAR) behind each number — including every trade as a full deal: who came in, who went out, and the net. Players-to-be-named, cash-only pieces, and three-team deals reconstruct imperfectly and may show partial legs.

Draft class report cards. Pick a club and a year to see the entire class — every selection, in order, with career WAR to date. "↻" marks players who didn't sign and were re-drafted later; their value credits the club that signed them.

The farm as an asset factory. A system earns credit two ways: promoting its own players into big-league production, and minting the trade capital that buys established stars — prospects spent in deals who produce for the acquiring club are farm successes, not failures. Homegrown = WAR that players this organization originally drafted or signed produced for it. Capital = WAR those originals produced for the clubs that traded for them, even when the deal itself predates 2015 — acquisition history is back-filled through the 2000s via MLB’s log and Retrosheet. The sliders window seasons: every number counts only production inside the window. Rating is the windowed percentile of homegrown + capital on the 20–80 scale.

Head to head. Any two organizations, every channel. Bars share a scale per row; red means negative.

Value imported since the 2014–15 offseason, counted only while the player stayed. Pre-debut = traded for as a minor leaguer. Reclamation = minor-league deals or players signed within ~13 months of being cut. A player who re-signs with the club he never left stays credited to his original acquisition.

Do your trades add value or bleed it? Gained = what your trade pickups produced for you. Surrendered = what the players you traded away produced for their new clubs. Full deal-by-deal detail lives in Team ledgers.

The fairness adjustment. Expected WAR is what average clubs produced from the same pick slots (2015–21 classes). Surplus is value above the seats you actually drafted from.

The international & amateur pipeline — players who debuted 2015 or later via signings outside the draft, counted with the signing club. Pool-restricted deals count here (Ohtani-to-Anaheim 2017); pro free agents do not (Ohtani-to-LA 2023).

What is each development machine built to do? The 2015–24 draft haul split by where the value was earned. Per-position detail for any club is in its Team ledger.

Late-round value — round 5 and later. After the pedigree rounds, the board belongs to the area scouts. Tap a club to see exactly who it found back there.

Accountability for premium picks. Top-15 selections from 2015–2021 still under 2.0 career WAR. Tap a club to see its misses; some are injury stories, but at these slots the industry counts them all.

The Originals — a no-movement universe. Every player stays forever with the organization that first acquired him: the club that drafted him (2000–2025), signed him as an international or undrafted amateur, or gave him his first MLB contract. Prospects traded before debuting credit their first org. The table shows what each franchise's originals are producing in 2026 and the record that talent would support — replacement level is ~48 wins per 162, pro-rated from the games played at build time. Raw WAR, so slumps and injuries count. Rosters are uneven by design; this is a scoreboard of who talent actually belongs to.

The best team money can buy. Set a payroll and the optimizer assembles the highest-WAR legal 26-man roster from every 2026 player: one at each infield spot and catcher, three outfielders, a DH, four bench bats, and thirteen pitchers, maximizing this season's WAR under your budget. Salaries are Baseball-Reference's listed 2026 figures; unlisted pre-arb players are priced at the $780K minimum, and deferred or backloaded deals use the listed number, so some superstars are bargains. Projected record uses the same replacement baseline as the Originals tab. Heuristic optimizer — near-optimal, not certified. Fair warning: pre-arbitration salaries are so low that even a ~$25M budget buys a 162-win-pace roster — that gap between pay and production is the entire economics of team building, and it's why the record chip caps at 162–0. Watch the Team WAR chip to see what each extra $100M actually buys.

Prospect comps. Every qualified minor leaguer this season, matched against twenty seasons of same-level history by statistical shape — K%, BB%, power, production, speed, all normalized within league-season — with age versus level weighted heaviest. Each comp is scored on WAR through his first six MLB seasons and mapped to the 2–8 role scale (R8 elite · R7 frequent All-Star · R6 occasional All-Star · R5 solid everyday or mid-rotation · R4 role player · R3 up-and-down · R2 organizational). A prospect's projection comes from his 25 nearest matured comps (seasons through __MAT__, so their six years are in): the grade is the highest role at least 26% of the cohort reached, tagged Poor (0–25) · Fair (26–49) · Good (50–74) · Excellent (75–100) by that probability. This is a triage tool built from public stat lines: it can't see swings, defense, makeup, or medicals — it points eyes and quantifies priors.

Draft value by home state. Every drafted player (2000–2025 classes, 0.5+ WAR) grouped by the state he grew up in — the area scout's territory cut. School shown on each row; HS/COL/JC inferred from age on draft day. The feed doesn't publish school locations, so college products credit their home state, not their campus.

All 780 active-roster players, classified by how their club got them, with the WAR each has produced for that club (2015–present, both stints for returnees). Deadline snapshot as of the build; use Refresh to re-pull live rosters — brand-new movers show as "Recent move" until the next full rebuild.

Method: every player-season is attributed to the most recent transaction that brought him to that club; value is clipped at zero per player-acquisition (roster WAR column shown raw). Data — MLB Stats API (drafts, transactions, rosters) joined on MLBAM ID to Baseball-Reference daily WAR files. Original computation; figures re-verifiable from public sources.
